title: oxvba-debug crate: consumer-facing debug handle architecture
description:
Stand up a new oxvba-debug crate as the consumer-facing debug API home: the borrow-bound !Send DebugSession in oxvba-host becomes oxvba-debug::DebugSessionCore on a worker thread, fronted by a Send + Sync + 'static DebugSessionHandle with an event stream (Stopped / Output / Continued / Exited / BreakpointChanged / ModuleLoaded / ThreadStarted). One architecture, three downstream consumers: OxIde (oxide-wf81 unblock), future oxvba-dap, future oxvba-cli debug.

Workset: docs/worksets/WORKSET_2026-05-23_OXVBA_DEBUG_HANDLE_ARCHITECTURE.md
Source handoff: ../OxIde/docs/HANDOFF_W391_DEBUGGER_COCKPIT.md (W391 review F1)
Downstream blocker: OxIde/oxide-wf81 (Persistent DnaOxideDebugSessionState)

Beads B00-B15 are children of this epic. Sequence is roughly linear with B08 (compiler source maps) as the only one that touches a sibling crate (oxvba-compiler). Public API freezes at B00 closure.

Out of scope (separate worksets):
- oxvba-dap crate and DAP protocol implementation
- OxIde adapter rewrite (tracked in OxIde/oxide-wf81)
- DAP-over-TCP / remote debugging
- oxvba-cli debug REPL
- Conditional breakpoints, hit counts, exception breakpoints, edit-and-continue (architecture must not preclude; separate feature work)

title: B09 - COM apartment management for the worker
description:
DebugAttachConfig::com_apartment (Sta / Mta / None) honored on the worker: CoInitializeEx on startup, CoUninitialize on shutdown (#[cfg(windows)]); None path works cross-platform. Worker initializes COM before constructing the core. Apartment verified from inside the worker via test-only DebugCommand::ReportWorkerApartment (test-thread CoGetApartmentType is not acceptable evidence because apartment state is thread-local).

V1 STA support is explicitly bounded to synchronous in-apartment COM work. Future cross-apartment callbacks / event sinks require a pumped wait loop (MsgWaitForMultipleObjects) before STA claims broaden. Hosts needing callbacks today should use Mta or None unless they own an external pump.

Closure: Sta/Mta/None all supported; STA scope bound documented; cross-platform CI covers apartment-relevant subset.

Source: workset B09.

title: B10 - Async surface (*_async variants, feature = tokio)
description:
Every sync handle method has an *_async variant returning the same typed output. Async subscribers use a tokio-friendly receiver over the same sequenced event stream. Worker stays sync (no internal tokio runtime); async is purely a caller-side ergonomic. Cancellation: dropping the future drops the oneshot receiver; worker discards the result when it finishes processing (no panic; logged).

Closure: async wrappers exist for every command; cancellation safe; no worker poisoning.

Source: workset B10.

title: B11 - Lifecycle, detach, and error propagation
description:
Attach failure / detach / drop-all-handles / mid-session worker error all handled deterministically. attach_debug_session returns Err(DebugAttachError) on compile/prepare failure with no worker left running. handle.detach() consumes one clone, joins only when it owns the last strong reference; returns DebugError::OutstandingHandles { count } otherwise. Last Arc<HandleInner> drop triggers Shutdown automatically. In-flight commands during Shutdown return SessionAlreadyDetached. Worker panic caught by catch_unwind, recorded; subsequent calls return WorkerFailed { stage, message }; handle unusable but not deadlocked.

Closure: all lifecycle scenarios pinned; no leaked workers, fds, COM apartments.

Source: workset B11.
acceptance_criteria: Attach failure leaves no worker running and returns DebugAttachError; explicit detach, drop-all-handles, in-flight shutdown, worker panic, and reattach scenarios are deterministic and typed; outstanding clones return DebugError::OutstandingHandles { count }; resource counters show no leaked workers/fds/COM apartments.

title: B03 - Move debug core and domain types into oxvba-debug
description:
Borrow-bound oxvba_host::DebugSession<'engine> becomes owned oxvba_debug::DebugSessionCore. All current debugger-domain types (DebugWatchRecord/Evaluation/Status, DebugBreakpointRecord/BindingStatus/UnresolvedReason, DebugPauseState (renamed from DebugVariantPauseState), DebugFrameVariant*, run results, DebugSessionError, DebugEvaluationRequest, DebugVariantEvaluationResult, DebugSessionCommandStatus) move with it.

DebugSessionCore owns Arc<Engine>, ProjectManifest, ProjectRuntimeSession; it does not borrow Engine. Explicitly !Send / !Sync. Engine::prepare_debug_session is removed; replacement is oxvba_debug::prepare_debug_session_core(Arc<Engine>, ...).

oxvba-host no longer contains a public debugger facade and has no dependency on oxvba-debug. No semantic change.

Closure: DebugSessionCore and all listed types live in oxvba-debug; oxvba-host has no debugger facade; no semantic regression.

title: Project object field layout and reference teardown: per-instance fields for Class_Terminate cascades
description:
## Outcome

Delivery bead: make regular project-class fields real per-instance storage on the runtime object, and make object-reference fields release deterministically through `Class_Terminate` teardown.

This bead is the object-field/reference half of the earlier broad "A" item. It deliberately does not close the VM activation-frame/recursion work; that residual is tracked separately.

## Current failure

`pure_oxvba_class_terminate_cascades_through_object_field` is ignored because `Parent` terminates but its regular field `mChild As Child` does not cascade. The field state is currently approximated through rewritten module/instance side paths and/or `withevents_bindings`, while the terminating runtime object box is dropped and then `Me` is rematerialized. That means ordinary fields are not owned by the live instance box at teardown time.

Related symptoms that remain outside this bead:
- `recursion_preserves_caller_locals`: flat register slots are reused by recursive calls.
- `gMT` trailing `T`: function return temporaries remain pinned by the flat return slot.

## Required behavior

For a project class instance, ordinary declared fields must be owned by the instance. When the last external reference to that instance is released:
1. the original instance is parked, not freed;
2. `Class_Terminate` runs with `Me` bound to that same parked instance so its fields are still readable;
3. if `Class_Terminate` resurrects `Me`, the instance is unparked and remains alive with terminate-once state;
4. otherwise the instance releases its owned fields and WithEvents subscriptions, cascading termination to any child objects that reach refcount zero, then frees the box.

## Scope

- `oxvba-runtime::ObjectRef` / `CompatObjectBase`: add an internal project-instance field store and parked/terminating/terminated state needed for same-box teardown.
- Runtime class/field metadata: carry stable class field identities/layouts for class module fields, including object-reference fields and scalar fields needed by existing rewrites.
- VM project dynamic object dispatch: get/set ordinary fields through `ObjectRef -> CompatObjectBase` rather than `withevents_bindings` or an `instance_id` side table.
- VM termination drain: stop rematerializing `Me` with a fresh box; drain parked project instances and release fields after termination only when the object was not resurrected.
- Compiler project lowering: distinguish ordinary class fields from genuine `WithEvents` bindings; remove the injected `__oxvba_withevents_clear_owner` dependency as the plain-field cleanup mechanism.
- Safety: keep this limited to OxVba project-instance compat objects. Foreign COM objects continue to release through their COM server and must not enter the parking queue.

## Non-goals

- Per-call activation frames, recursive call slot windows, ByRef frame aliases, and debugger frame snapshots.
- Full front-end/binder replacement.
- Tracing cycle collection; project object cycles remain reference-count leaks, matching VBA expectations.
design:
## Fresh-eyes review findings folded into this bead

1. The earlier bead shape mixed per-instance object fields with activation frames. This bead is intentionally the object-field/reference half; recursion frames and the `gMT` return-slot lifetime residual stay in `bd-xkwq`.
2. Termination must run against the original object box. Rematerializing `Me` as a fresh compat object preserves only the numeric identity and loses the owned field graph needed for `Class_Terminate` reads and cascaded release.
3. Resurrection must be checked before clearing fields. A resurrected object is marked terminate-once and unparked with its fields/subscriptions intact; a non-resurrected object clears owned fields after `Class_Terminate` and then frees the box.
4. Ordinary fields and genuine `WithEvents` bindings need separate ownership. Plain fields are object-owned values; `WithEvents` still owns event subscription state until that model is replaced.
5. The runtime lane is single-threaded. Live `ObjectRef` is not a cross-thread handle; shared COM/callback surfaces store raw identity/projection tokens and reconstruct edge handles instead of requiring `ObjectRef: Send + Sync`.

## Implemented layout

Use stable class-state binding tokens as the field layout key for ordinary project-class fields:
- `ProjectDynamicObjectRoute.field_tokens` records ordinary declared class field tokens for the route.
- `CompatObjectBase` owns a single-threaded `RefCell<BTreeMap<i32, Variant>>` field store keyed by those tokens. This is intentionally token-keyed rather than string/global/route storage; field reads and writes go through the receiver object identity.
- `IntrinsicWithEventsGet/Set` continues to serve both old lowering paths, but the VM first checks whether the owner is a project instance and the token is an ordinary field token. If so, it reads/writes the object-owned field store. Only genuine WithEvents tokens use `withevents_bindings` and subscription sync.
- Compiler lowering writes ordinary fields through the runtime setter without assigning the setter result back to the field name, avoiding an extra procedure/module slot reference that would pin object fields past the owning instance.

## Parking and teardown

Project-instance compat objects carry explicit lifecycle state: alive, parked, running termination, and terminated. At the last release of a terminating project instance, `compat_release` parks the original box in a thread-local termination queue instead of freeing it. The VM drain retains that same box for `Me`, invokes `Class_Terminate`, then calls `finish_pending_termination` regardless of whether the terminate body succeeded. If the object was resurrected, it is unparked and remains alive with terminate-once state; otherwise fields are cleared, releasing child object edges and cascading pending terminations, then the box is freed.

`reset_pending_terminations` also respects live references: it does not free a parked box whose refcount was raised, and it clears the parked state so a later final release can free normally without re-running terminate.

## Residuals outside this bead

`recursion_preserves_caller_locals` and the `gMT` trailing `T` remain activation-frame/return-slot lifetime work under `bd-xkwq`. They are not field-layout failures.
acceptance_criteria:
Close when all are true:

- `pure_oxvba_class_terminate_cascades_through_object_field` is unignored and passes with log `1PC2`.
- A per-instance field isolation test proves two instances do not share ordinary field storage and field reads/writes go through object identity, not route/global state.
- `Class_Terminate` uses the parked original object as `Me`; no fresh-box rematerialization is used to access fields during teardown.
- Resurrection is handled coherently: terminate-once state is recorded, resurrected objects are not freed or field-cleared, and non-resurrected objects release fields/subscriptions and cascade child terminations.
- `withevents_bindings` is not used as ordinary-field storage; genuine WithEvents behavior remains covered by existing tests.
- Live project `ObjectRef` values are not exposed as cross-thread `Send`/`Sync` runtime objects; any affected host/debug/snapshot surfaces use projections or explicit future marshalling instead.
- Relevant checks pass: at minimum `cargo test -p oxvba-runtime -p oxvba-vm -p oxvba-host pure_oxvba_class_terminate --quiet` plus any compiler tests touched by field metadata/lowering changes.
- Fresh-eyes review records no remaining material issues in field ownership, same-box teardown, resurrection order, or accidental cross-thread live-object sharing.

Explicit residuals not required for this bead closure:
- `recursion_preserves_caller_locals` remains ignored until activation frames land.
- `gMT` trailing terminate remains activation-frame/return-slot work and must stay documented as such.

title: CORE-1 seal VbaRecord layouts and field access
description: Outcome: seal VbaRecord layout construction and field access so no safe public API can form an out-of-bounds/misaligned pointer or a wrapped/overlapping record layout. Effect: delivery. Clauses: CONF-QUALITY-001|RUNTIME-VALUE-001|SEC-BOUNDARY-001. Canonical matrix row: CORE-READINESS/CORE-BASELINE-UNSAFE-CLIPPY. The bd-59co.2.2.2 audit confirmed that publicly constructible VbaRecordFieldLayout values can be passed to safe field_ptr/field_mut_ptr, whose unchecked ptr.add relies on false membership assumptions, and that unchecked align_to addition can wrap near usize::MAX before later checked_add validation. Seal or validate field handles, use checked alignment/stride/size arithmetic throughout nested/fixed layouts, make allocation failure bounded/fallible, and audit every trusted offset consumer. Acceptance commands: command:cargo test -p oxvba-runtime vba_record_layout_sealing -- --nocapture; command:cargo test -p oxvba-runtime vba_record -- --nocapture; command:cargo clippy -p oxvba-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings. Residual behavior: descriptor/session architecture remains related to CORE-5 rollout bd-59co.2.7.1; this bead must not preserve a safe raw-pointer escape based on caller discipline. Fresh-eyes Sol review is required.
acceptance_criteria: VbaRecord layout arithmetic is checked end-to-end; hostile near-usize fixed-string/nested/fixed-array shapes fail without panic or allocation; safe callers cannot forge or use a foreign-layout field handle to reach ptr.add; a handle is an immutable layout capability and may be reused only across records sharing that exact Arc layout, including after the source record drops; valid x64 offsets/layout remain exact; all construction/clone/drop metadata traversal is bounded or allocation-free after sealed admission; focused tests, strict Clippy, Miri and balance checks pass; any required public migration is documented and reviewed.
notes: Architecture adjudication during fresh-eyes review: VbaRecordFieldHandle is intentionally bound to one immutable Arc<VbaRecordLayout>, not one record instance. It contains no data pointer, owns the Arc, and destination projection recomputes the pointer after full checks. Same-layout cross-record reuse is valid and must be positively tested, including after the originating record drops; independently constructed structurally equal layouts are foreign and must fail before pointer arithmetic.
close_reason: Delivered sealed read-only layouts and immutable Arc-layout field capabilities; foreign/forged handles fail before pointer arithmetic while same-layout reuse is proved across record lifetimes. Checked arithmetic, 64KiB/60-rank admission, fixed-array shape rejection, cycle/depth/visit bounds, fallible construction, allocation-free Drop and metadata-clone removal are tested. title: A2 gate hardening: typed consumption-status and gap-classification enums
description:
@
A2 gate hardening + production strict flip + in-memory upgrade. (1) Typed consumption-status/gap enums (replace "unsupported-rejected" magic string + substring gap matching); hard error on unknown seed-table values. (2) Make the strict gate CONTENT-BASED not origin-based: drop the blanket PACKAGE-INMEMORY-NOT-STRICT reason; keep section-completeness checks; VmPackageOrigin becomes informational. (3) Add a complete in-memory package builder (compile_source_to_bundle: source -> one-module manifest -> compile_project -> OxBundle::from_compiled_project, held in memory). (4) FLIP strict gate onto ALL production execution/invoke paths and REMOVE the non-strict compatibility bypass; migrate ~20 OxBundle::new/VmExecutionPackage::new sites (incl. host execute_source_* engine.rs:1108 and wrapper_plan.rs:451) to the complete builder; fold preflight_host_sensitive_support into the support report. Keep incomplete minimal constructors only for tests that verify rejection. Consequence: unsupported-classified lanes hard-reject in production until their lane bead closes. Largely absorbs Workset B (bd-dpmy) delivery beads .2-.4.

## Success Criteria
- Typed gap/status enums; unknown seed-table value is a hard error.
- Strict gate judges by section completeness; a complete in-memory package is fully supported; origin is informational.
- compile_source_to_bundle builds a complete strict package; host snippet + VM free fns route through it.
- No production path executes a package without the strict gate; no non-strict public execution bypass remains.
- Full suite run through the strict gate; new rejections enumerated and mapped to owning lane beads.
@

title: Compiler: support 'New <Class>' as an expression (e.g. Set t = New Ticker, withevents-set arg)
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Compile an active-project source-class program where a value-producing New expression appears in expression position, especially Set obj = New Widget and WithEvents Set src = New Emitter paths that previously rewrote through __oxvba_withevents_set(..., New Ticker).

## Current/Original Failure
Legacy parse_expr did not support New <Class> as a nested expression, so helper-rewritten WithEvents Set arguments could fail as unsupported statement/source. Dim As New declaration initialization was separate and already worked.

Accepted active-project New <Class> expression forms route through HIR/project-aware construction binding, emit project object-reference bytecode, preserve helper-free source artifacts for audited production paths, and prove WithEvents source-class construction without depending on legacy parse_expr support for arbitrary nested New expressions.

title: Activation-frame model + object lifetime (full "A"): per-call frames to fix recursion and Class_Terminate teardown
description:
## Root cause

The VM uses a single FLAT GLOBAL register file (`RegisterFile.registers: Vec<RuntimeSlot>`);
`call_stack` saves only `(return_pc, error_frame)`. There are NO per-call activation frames /
slot windows: emit assigns every procedure''s locals/params/temps distinct GLOBAL slot indices
(`next_slot` in emit.rs), and a callee writes into those same global slots. This single missing
mechanism (activation frames) is the root cause of two symptom families.

## Symptoms

1. RECURSION IS BROKEN. A recursive callee reuses the caller''s slots, clobbering locals.
   Verified: `Fact(5)` returns 16, not 120. Probe: `recursion_preserves_caller_locals`
   (`#[ignore]`d in `crates/oxvba-host/tests/com_early_project_end_to_end.rs`). This is a
   conformance correctness gap (VBA supports recursion).

2. OBJECT-SLOT LIFETIME. Object references linger in global slots because nothing pops a frame,
   so a dropped reference never reaches refcount 0:
   - Cascade through a regular (non-WithEvents) object field: owner terminates (`1P2`) but the
     child is retained beyond the per-instance binding. Test
     `pure_oxvba_class_terminate_cascades_through_object_field` (`#[ignore]`d, expects `1PC2`).
   - `gMT` trailing-`T`: a function-returned temporary is pinned by the callee''s RETURN SLOT
     until the next call (so end-of-statement terminate does not fire).
   - General Me-param / return-slot / field-state-slot retention.

## Fix direction

Introduce per-call ACTIVATION FRAMES (a frame base / slot window pushed on call, popped on
return): slot indices become FRAME-RELATIVE; each call gets a fresh frame; on return the frame is
released, dropping its object references. This makes recursion correct AND brings object lifetimes
to VBA-correct teardown timing in one mechanism.

## Scope

- VM (`oxvba-vm/interpreter.rs`, `register_file.rs`): frame stack + frame-base register;
  `CallProc`/`Return` and the inline/`invoke_*_with_slots` paths push/pop frames.
- Emit (`oxvba-compiler/emit.rs`): allocate frame-relative slots per procedure.
- Slot-semantics CONTRACT CHANGE (instruction format unchanged): coordinate with the front-end
  rework — see `docs/worksets/WORKSET_2026-05-31_FRONTEND_TOKENIZER_PARSER_BINDER_AST_REFACTOR.md`
  §6.1 (Phase 4+ lowering must emit frame-relative slots).
- Preserve the existing Class_Terminate statement/epilogue drain (commit 8c082e2c) and Excel
  timing oracle.

## Acceptance criteria

- Un-ignore and pass `recursion_preserves_caller_locals` (`Fact(5) == 120`).
- Un-ignore and pass `pure_oxvba_class_terminate_cascades_through_object_field` (`1PC2`).
- Restore the `gMT` trailing-`T` (probe B of the oracle): the function-returned temporary
  terminates at end of statement.
- Full regression green (compiler 861+, vm, host, conformance) + Excel timing oracle unchanged.

## References

- Front-end workset §6.1 (slot-contract dependency).
- `docs/evidence/conformance/CLASS_TERMINATE_TIMING_ORACLE_2026-05-31.md`.
- Memory: project_objects_refcounted_iunknown (the standing "A" follow-up).
- This is the "A" item parked during the Class_Terminate cascade design decision.

title: M4 Cranelift JIT: typed OxIR -> native x64, vm3 as oracle
description:
Outcome: the second runtime of the north star (one front-end -> typed .oxi OxImage -> two runtimes): a Cranelift JIT that compiles the full OxIR vocabulary to native x64, matches vm3 (the oracle) on all six differential axes over the full corpus, then adds typed fast paths (Phase B), JIT-generated COM interface vtable implementations, and the AOT PE export path. Authoritative plan: docs/OXVBA_JIT_PLAN.md (committed 8c5939b3) - architecture, decision histories, worksets M4-0..M4-14, risk register.

Fixed principles (plan section 0): vm3 is the executable spec; shared runtime behind extern "C" shims, NOT vm3's frame/slot machine; typed everywhere the IR is typed (Variant machinery only where the language is genuinely dynamic); no native exceptions - faults are i32 status returns; Phase A commits to the same typed value model Phase B inlines; no silent fallback ever (clean whole-program Unsupported + monotone jit_scope ratchet; mixed execution only under jit-debug for bisection).

title: M4-8 Objects, classes, lifecycle, project events
description:
Outcome: the project object model compiles, with Terminate timing (a differential axis) and drain re-entrancy proven - Class_Terminate bodies run as COMPILED code re-entered through ProcInvoker. Size L.

Tasks: (1) NewObject/NewExtern, predeclared singletons (Predeclared/PredeclaredExtern + Set variants), instance ids via ExecState. (5) AddRef/Release{may_terminate}: enqueue-only (O6). (6) DrainTerminations: rt_maybe_drain fixpoint through ProcInvoker under the shared draining guard - compiled Terminate bodies re-enter natively. (7) Project RaiseEvent -> WithEvents fan-out over the shared event-route tables in ExecState (handlers via ProcInvoker).

title: M4-4 Control flow, typed calling convention, ByRef, stack guard
description:
Outcome: typed primary entries become the convention of record (plan section 6 - the Variant-argv shape is a rejected draft; decision history recorded there); late binding goes through generated dynamic-entry thunks. Size M-L.

Tasks: (1) Branch/Jump lowering + loop shapes (Branch cond is pre-computed Boolean - no fallible truthiness in the terminator). (2) Typed primary entry per OxFunc, signature derived from locals[0..param_count]: ByVal scalars by-value machine registers (i32/i64/f32/f64, Bool i8, Currency i64); ByVal Variant/owning by pointer with callee clone-in (O8); ByRef = *mut typed slot (scalars at the caller's escaped machine-typed slot; String/Object/Array/Record at the bare-handle slot - exactly BSTR*/IUnknown** shapes; Variant at the 16-byte slot); return via typed out-pointer (dead-on-entry, O2 - keeps entries callable from Rust shims over plain C ABI); i32 status is the sole register return. Me receiver: mirror vm3's class-method call path exactly (flagged implementation-time confirmation in the plan). (3) Omitted args reach only Variant params (binder guarantees it - caller-side defaults): caller passes MISSING_ARG scratch, callee writes discarded (vm3 parity). (4) ParamArray: one array argument (binder boxes the tail); element-alias copy-out caller-side via the shared VariantChanged-guarded helper (per the M4-1 confirmation). (5) Dynamic-entry thunk generator: per-function uniform adapter unboxing/coercing argv to machine types with vm3's late-bound coercion semantics (err 13 on mismatch, via shared coerce helpers), calling the typed entry, boxing the result. Consumers: CallByName, late-bound member dispatch, Property Get/Let/Set resolution, ProcInvoker, unproven CallProcRef. (6) Static dispatch typed: CallProc/CallExtern direct typed calls; CallProcRef typed-indirect where the signature is statically known, else dynamic entry via fn tables. Bring-up may route static calls through dynamic entries first, switching to typed calls within this workset - an optimization inside one architecture, never a migration. (7) Activation save/restore correct across calls (R1/R2). (8) err-28 stack guard: prologue watermark check against ctx.stack_limit -> seat err 28 + return ST_FAULT BEFORE frame_enter (catchable VBA fault, NEVER a cranelift trap); dedicated big-stack thread (~64MB) for compiled runs; match vm3's frame-depth ceiling constant for parity.

Verify: control/call corpus slices green THROUGH TYPED ENTRIES; late-bound corpus programs green through dynamic entries; a deep-recursion program raises err 28 identically on both engines (promote vm3's test shape to a corpus program).

title: M4-5 Error model compilation (R1-R14)
description:
Outcome: the full VBA error/Resume/GoSub model compiles per plan section 3, sharing the ErrEngine with vm3; the error-family corpus (the largest thematic slice) is the gate. Size L.

Tasks: (1) Fault-code convention on every fallible op and call site: brif ok / ST_HALT -> cleanup_epilogue(HALT) / ST_FAULT -> the block's fault pad (which IS R2 default propagation at call statements). (2) FaultDispatch pad lowering: call rt_route_fault(state, idx(resume), idx(resume_next)) -> switch DISP_UNWIND -> epilogue(ST_FAULT) | DISP_RESUME_NEXT -> STATIC jump to resume_next | DISP_HANDLER -> load dispatch_target -> redispatch. (3) Per-function compact dispatch table T = sort(H u S u G) (H = SetErrorHandler(GotoLabel) targets, S = FaultDispatch seeds, G = GoSub returns) + ONE redispatch block: i32 block-param br_table over T, default -> trap (compiler bug caught loudly; full-block tables rejected - they hide corrupt indices). (4) Resume/ResumeNext terminators: rt_resume checks active_error (empty -> err 20 via this block's own pad), resets Err, clears the latch, RE-ARMS the caught handler policy, returns the seed index -> redispatch; Resume <label> = same helper then a static jump. (5) On Error mode sets via helper (R5 Err auto-reset makes SetErrorHandler a helper, not inline). (6) GoSub: push idx(ret) onto the activation gosub stack (unbounded LIFO, R12), static jump; GoSubReturn: pop (empty -> err 3 via pad) -> redispatch. (7) Erl (inline load/store on the cached activation), Err.Raise defaults + inheritance (R11), R10 Exit clears Err, R13 On Error GoTo -1 (clear active-error latch keep handler), R14 End = ST_HALT bypassing handlers, no drain. (8) Cross-frame unwinding: callee runs cleanup epilogue + leave_activation BEFORE returning ST_FAULT so the caller's cells are restored when its pad dispatches; driver-level ST_FAULT = host terminate boundary.

Verify: the ENTIRE error-family corpus green on all axes; error_loop bench recorded (the per-fallible-op branch tax quantified early, feeding risk 3).

title: Compiler: lower logical/comparison operators and Not as expression rvalues; support type-suffix literals
description:
@
Coverage testing (bd-eura.4) surfaced compiler typecheck/emit front-end gaps (NOT VM gaps; the VM has these capabilities). Fix in crates/oxvba-compiler typecheck/emit lowering.

1) Logical & comparison operators + Not as assignment-expression rvalues fail to compile in BOTH pipelines (lightweight compile_with_runtime_metadata and full compile_project): "t = a And b", "t = a Or b", "t = Not a", "t = (1 = 1)" -> TypeError("unsupported statement: ..."). They DO work as branch predicates (If a And b Then ...).
2) Type-suffix numeric literals: "d = d * 2#" (Double #-suffix) -> unsupported statement.
3) Statement-form member calls on objects: "L.Wire" / "L.Trigger 42" (no-paren / statement call on an As New source-class object) -> "call to unknown procedure: l_wire". Function-call form "c.Add(3,4)" works (INTP-016). This blocks positive source-class event flow (Event/RaiseEvent -> WithEvents handler), which otherwise needs only this member-call lowering.

All core VBA expression/statement forms; found via crates/oxvba-vm/tests/vm_feature_coverage.rs and an attempted source-event-flow host test.
close_reason: All three compiler front-end gaps fixed: (1) logical And/Or/Not as expression rvalues (commit 6f51f3cf), (2) type-suffix numeric literals (8afab016), (3) bare statement-form member calls (this commit). Fresh-eyes: 858 compiler lib tests + full host integration suite pass (Access/ADO flake passes on rerun); clippy -D warnings + fmt clean; bare member-call rewrite gated by member-resolution so module-qualified/builtin dotted statements unaffected. New tests: vm_feature_coverage (logical rvalues, precedence, type-suffix) + source_member_call_statements. Two deeper pre-existing gaps surfaced and filed separately (bd-7ins object field state, bd-asrd New-expression).

title: Refactor built-in library: split native- vs VBA-implemented bodies + rationalize
description:
DEFERRED until the vm3-vs-spec gap-closure (epic bd-4ktq) is complete. Design note: docs/BUILTIN_LIBRARY_NATIVE_VS_VBA_SPLIT.md.

The builtins-as-library program (memory project_builtins_as_library, COMPLETE) made the whole VBA built-in surface resolve as a synthetic 'VBA' library bundle, but EVERY body is still native Rust (NativeImplId/NativeMethodId). The bundle already supports VBA-bytecode bodies too. Idea: split the bodies into (1) NATIVE-kept (host/OS, codecs, Format engine, coercion/numeric primitives, exact Currency/Decimal, CreateObject/GetObject, special forms + structural intrinsics) and (2) VBA-IMPLEMENTED for pure compositions (IsDate->CDate, Partition, FormatNumber/Currency/Percent/DateTime, financial IPmt/PPmt/SLN/SYD/DDB, RGB/QBColor, WeekdayName/MonthName) — written as real VBA source in the bundle, correct-by-construction + JIT-uniform + self-testing. Prime targets = the Absent functions from the gap audit.

Then rationalize: delete the dead keyless oxvba-lib Collection first-cut if still present; fix stale oxvba-lib Collection doc comments; consolidate the scattered LibError/CollectionError/HalError->VBA-error-number maps into one table (audit items hal-errors-flattened-to-5, collection-keynotfound-error-9-not-5, sparse-default-error-message); unify $-suffix vs non-$ return typing + Null-propagation in the shared dispatch.

Open design Qs (in the note): where VBA source bodies live + build-time compilation into the &'static bundle; bootstrap/cycle guards; hot-path perf (frame cost vs the native call_extern shortcut); Err.Number fidelity from VBA-raised bodies.

title: vm3 perf: dynamic-array element access is O(N) → array loops O(N²) (OxForms handover)
description: From OxForms (docs/handovers/HANDOVER_OxVba_vm3_dynamic_array_access_perf.md). On vm3 (enable_jit=false), reading arr(i) of a module-level dynamic array inside a loop is O(N) in array length, so array loops are O(N^2): 100-elem loop=130ms, 400-elem=2.2s (native ~1us). Isolated to the element read (ScanArray vs ScanPlain). Suspect a per-access SafeArray/array-Variant deep-clone or descriptor walk in the vm3 array-index load path. Make element access O(1). First look: oxvba-vm3 OxInst array load/store + oxvba-runtime safe_array.rs element accessor + module-field place resolution. Perf gap, independent of the bd-4ktq correctness sweep. OxForms will re-run their bench after the fix.

title: Epic: internal COM projection core
description: Delivery epic for the internal COM projection core. Scope is the runtime substrate that lets one object identity expose IUnknown, IDispatch, custom dual interfaces, source/event interfaces, and future host-call projections without duplicating lifetime or descriptor truth.

Implement in oxvba-runtime, likely object_ref.rs plus a com_projection module, preserving Variant/ObjectRef binary/value behavior. Keep Windows-specific COM APIs out of runtime; represent GUIDs and projections portably.

description: Delivery bead to split runtime object identity from interface projection. Outcome: ObjectRef remains the value carrier, but runtime can represent 'this object as this interface' with one shared identity/lifetime record.
design: Expected before: ObjectRef wraps raw IUnknown-like identity/compat handles and carries optional class descriptors; interface projection is implicit. Implement RuntimeObjectIdentity and RuntimeInterfaceProjection records or equivalent, with stable object id, descriptor pointer/Arc, lifetime policy, apartment/thread metadata placeholder, and projection identity. Ensure QueryInterface-style paths return projections while Variant object storage, pointer helpers, SAFEARRAY object values, and existing compat identities keep behavior. Avoid rewriting all dynamic dispatch at once.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove multiple projections share the same IUnknown identity, ObjectRef clone/drop behavior and raw pointer helpers do not regress, Variant object roundtrips still work, and descriptor-backed dispatch plan cache still works for pure OxVba objects.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-runtime/src/object_ref.rs, variant.rs, safe_array.rs, pointer_helpers.rs; crates/oxvba-vm/src/semantics.rs object helpers; object ABI workset; downstream bd-wcs1.2.3/5/7/8.
close_reason: Completed: added RuntimeObjectIdentity/RuntimeInterfaceProjection records over ObjectRef, projection lookup by enum/GUID, shared-identity projection tests, and preserved existing Variant/ObjectRef behavior via full oxvba-runtime tests plus COM/VM checks.

title: Add descriptor-backed custom QueryInterface coverage
description: Delivery bead to prove descriptor-backed custom QueryInterface. Outcome: runtime raw QI can advertise and return custom interface projections, not just IUnknown/IDispatch-like known surfaces.
design: Expected before: descriptor_backed_object_supports_raw_query_interface_projection covers a baseline descriptor-backed projection. Extend RuntimeInterfaceDescriptor/identity so an object descriptor lists custom dual/source/connection interfaces. Raw QI should compare GUIDs, return a projection pointer/object handle with AddRef on success, return null/E_NOINTERFACE-equivalent on failure, and preserve IUnknown identity stability. Include failure and refcount balance tests, but do not require Windows DLL generation yet.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime tests cover QI success for custom IID, QI failure for unknown IID, AddRef/Release balance, IUnknown identity stability across IDispatch/custom projections, and no regression to existing descriptor cache tests.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-runtime/src/object_ref.rs tests; COM identity invariants from Win32/IUnknown; prerequisite for bd-wcs1.5.3, 7.1, 8.2.
close_reason: Completed: raw runtime QueryInterface now compares RuntimeGuid identities; tests cover custom IID success, unknown IID failure/null out, AddRef/Release balance, and shared IUnknown identity with full runtime plus COM/VM checks passing.

title: Epic: call descriptor call-frame and marshaling core
description: Delivery epic for the shared call descriptor, RuntimeCallFrame, result, and marshaling core. Scope is one canonical invocation representation shared by internal project calls, project dynamic dispatch, external COM IDispatch, dual-interface vtable stubs, event sink calls, and host UDF invocation.
design: Expected before: compiler bytecode carries project and imported COM member metadata, VM/host can invoke class members with Variants, and COM windows_invoke/windows_variant has adapter-specific marshaling. Implementation should avoid creating separate call paths for wrapper DLL, UDF, and events; instead introduce receiver/selector/args/named/property-put/byref/locale/context/error/result carriers, then route a bounded existing project-object slice through it before widening.
acceptance_criteria: RuntimeCallFrame/result types exist; one pure OxVba method/property/default-member path executes through the frame in VM/JIT/host tests; COM DISPPARAMS/VARIANT helpers consume/produce call frames; no regression to user-authored DispatchInvoke late/mixed-bound semantics.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-compiler/src/bytecode.rs, emit.rs, project.rs, resolve.rs, typecheck.rs; crates/oxvba-host/src/engine.rs; crates/oxvba-vm/src/interpreter.rs and semantics.rs; crates/oxvba-jit/src/cranelift.rs; crates/oxvba-com/src/windows_invoke.rs and windows_variant.rs. MS-OAUT anchors: GetIDsOfNames maps names to DISPIDs, Invoke uses DISPPARAMS, reverse rgvarg order, pVarResult/EXCEPINFO/pArgErr/byref obligations.
close_reason: Done: call-frame and marshaling core complete. RuntimeCallFrame/RuntimeCallResult landed in bd-wcs1.3.1; pure OxVba object invocation routes through runtime frames in bd-wcs1.3.2; COM DISPPARAMS/VARIANT marshaling helpers consume and produce call frames in bd-wcs1.3.3. Evidence across child closures includes cargo test -p oxvba-runtime call_frame --quiet, oxvba-host focused object invocation tests, cargo test -p oxvba-com --quiet, cargo check for runtime/host/com, and governance passing.

title: Introduce RuntimeCallFrame and call result abstractions
description: Delivery bead to introduce RuntimeCallFrame and call result abstractions. Outcome: a stable runtime-level invocation carrier exists for all later wrapper, event, and UDF call paths.
design: Expected before: member metadata exists, but callers pass ad hoc names/Variants/engine hooks. Add RuntimeCallFrame, RuntimeCallSelector, RuntimeCallKind, RuntimeCallArgument, RuntimeNamedArgument, RuntimeByRefSlot/Writeback, RuntimeCallContext, RuntimeCallResult, and RuntimeCallError as needed. Include selector forms for descriptor, DISPID, name, vtable slot, and host-call id. Model property put separately enough to satisfy DISPID_PROPERTYPUT later. Keep structures independent from Windows-only VARIANT pointers.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime unit tests cover construction, named/positional ordering, property get/let/set representation, byref writeback placeholders, locale/context fields, and error/result mapping. Public exports are available for compiler/host/com crates without circular dependencies.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-runtime/src/lib.rs and new call_frame module; ProjectMemberCallDescriptor in compiler bytecode; COMMemberCallDescriptor; MS-OAUT Invoke argument obligations; users bd-wcs1.3.2/3.3/5.3/8.2/9.2.
close_reason: Completed: introduced exported runtime call-frame/result/error/byref/context selector carriers with tests for ordering, property get/let/set, byref writebacks, locale/caller context, and result/error mapping; runtime, COM/VM/host checks and governance passed.

title: Route one project object slice through call-frame core
description: Delivery bead to route one pure OxVba object invocation slice through RuntimeCallFrame. Outcome: the call-frame core is executable, not just a data model, while preserving existing VM/JIT behavior.
design: Expected before: Engine::invoke_member_on_object_with_variants can invoke object members by name/Variants and pure OxVba descriptor cache tests exist. Pick a bounded class fixture covering method, property get/let/set, default/indexed member if feasible. Adapt host/VM dispatch to build RuntimeCallFrame, invoke through a shared thunk, and return RuntimeCallResult before converting back to existing Variant flow. Keep old path available until parity tests pass; do not widen to external COM yet.
acceptance_criteria: Host/compiler/VM/JIT tests prove method/property/default-member results match prior behavior, typed project-member metadata remains intact, explicit user DispatchInvoke remains late/mixed-bound, and cargo test -p oxvba-host relevant tests pass.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-host/src/engine.rs create_class_instance/invoke_member_on_object_with_variants; crates/oxvba-compiler tests around pure_oxvba_* descriptor cache; VM/JIT call proc handling; prerequisite for bd-wcs1.5.3 and 9.2.
close_reason: Completed: Engine object member invocation now builds RuntimeCallFrame and invokes through a frame thunk for the pure OxVba object path; host unit, invoke_procedure, pure OxVba COM-early project tests, project integration suite, runtime tests, cargo check, and governance passed.

title: Centralize COM DISPPARAMS and VARIANT marshaling over call frames
description: Delivery bead to centralize COM DISPPARAMS/VARIANT marshaling over call frames. Outcome: COM adapters convert into RuntimeCallFrame and RuntimeCallResult rather than duplicating wrapper-specific marshaling.
design: Expected before: oxvba-com windows_variant.rs and windows_invoke.rs know how to convert Windows VARIANTs and call external IDispatch, but generated server code would otherwise need its own marshaler. Implement helper APIs in oxvba-com for DISPPARAMS -> RuntimeCallFrame args, named arg DISPIDs including DISPID_PROPERTYPUT, reverse rgvarg order, byref slots/cVarRef/rgVarRefIdx, and RuntimeCallResult -> VARIANT/EXCEPINFO/HRESULT. Reuse existing COM datatype parity policy for unsupported carriers.
acceptance_criteria: oxvba-com tests cover positional/named/property-put order, byref writeback, pArgErr index selection, EXCEPINFO population for runtime errors, object/SAFEARRAY/unsupported type mapping, and cargo test -p oxvba-com passes. Generated DLL code can call these helpers later.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-com/src/windows_variant.rs, windows_invoke.rs, model.rs; COM datatype oracle evidence; MS-OAUT anchors CONF-0561/0575/0599/0614/0615/0617/0618/0620/0622/0623/0627/0629.
close_reason: Done: added oxvba-com Windows call-frame marshaling helpers for DISPPARAMS -> RuntimeCallFrame, RuntimeCallResult -> VARIANT, byref writebacks, logical-to-COM pArgErr mapping, and RuntimeCallError -> EXCEPINFO/HRESULT. Tests cover positional/named/property-put order, byref writeback, pArgErr selection, EXCEPINFO population, object and SAFEARRAY result mapping, unsupported VARIANT diagnostics, and empty results. Evidence: cargo test -p oxvba-com windows_call_frame --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-com --quiet; cargo check -p oxvba-com -p oxvba-runtime -p oxvba-host --quiet; ./scripts/check-governance.ps1.

title: Epic: bundle export metadata and build-target integration
description: Delivery epic for bundle export metadata and build-target integration. Scope is to persist all wrapper-facing descriptors in .oxb and expose BuildTarget=WrappedComServer through project parsing/generation/CLI/direct-host settings without reparsing source in generated wrappers.
design: Expected before: OxBundle contains bytecode/metadata for execution and current .basproj BuildTarget supports Bundle/WrapperExe/WrapperLibrary. Existing COM class metadata/typelib export scaffolding exists in oxvba-build but is not a full wrapper contract. Implementation should add versioned bundle metadata for exported classes/interfaces/events/host-callables and stable GUID/DISPID identities; then wire project/host surfaces to represent WrappedComServer and Windows-only capability/disabled reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Bundle serialization roundtrips descriptor metadata; parse/generate/host-helper tests cover BuildTarget=WrappedComServer and alias policy; CLI/direct-host surfaces expose the target without CLI text parsing; specs are updated.
notes: Pointers: OxBundle in crates/oxvba-compiler; crates/oxvba-project/src/model.rs, parse.rs, generate.rs, load.rs, host_helpers.rs; crates/oxvba-cli/src/main.rs; crates/oxvba-host/src/embedded.rs; docs/spec/OXVBA_EMBEDDED_BUILD_RUN_CONTRACT_V1.md.
close_reason: Done: bundle export metadata and build-target integration complete. bd-wcs1.4.1 added OxBundle v3 descriptor_inventory for COM classes/interfaces/members/events and host calls with v1/v2 compatibility; bd-wcs1.4.2 added BuildTarget=WrappedComServer parse/generate/direct-host support, alias normalization, and typed non-Windows status. Evidence: child closure test/check/governance evidence is recorded and pushed.

title: Persist COM and host-call descriptors in OxBundle
description: Delivery bead to persist COM and host-call descriptors in OxBundle. Outcome: generated wrappers and hosts can consume descriptor truth from .oxb without reparsing .bas/.cls source.
design: Expected before: OxBundle serializes executable bytecode/metadata and project objects have runtime descriptors in memory, but exported class/interface/event/UDF metadata is not a stable bundle section. Add versioned, backward-compatible metadata for TypeLibID, CLSIDs, IIDs, ProgIDs, class exposure/creatability, default/dual/source interfaces, members with DISPIDs/vtable slots/flags/param Automation types, event sources, and host-callable module functions. Prefer optional sections/defaults so old bundles remain readable or fail with clear version diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Serialization/deserialization roundtrip tests cover class/interface/member/event/host-call descriptors and stable IDs; old/minimal bundle tests still pass; descriptors are available to oxvba-build/host without source reparse; docs mention compatibility policy.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-compiler OxBundle definitions/usages; crates/oxvba-cli bundle writes; crates/oxvba-launcher bundle reads; docs/spec/BUILD_TARGET_AND_WRAPPER_BOUNDARY_V1.md wrapper boundary contract.
close_reason: Done: OxBundle format v3 now persists descriptor_inventory with COM class/interface/member descriptors, COM event descriptors, and host-call descriptors with deterministic stable IDs. Version 1 and version 2 bundle deserialization upgrade paths remain covered, and CLI build enrichment copies validated COM ProgID/Instancing/description metadata into the bundle descriptors. Docs record the descriptor-inventory compatibility policy. Evidence: cargo test -p oxvba-compiler bundle --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-compiler --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-cli --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-build com_attribute_export --quiet; cargo check -p oxvba-compiler -p oxvba-cli -p oxvba-host -p oxvba-build --quiet; ./scripts/check-governance.ps1.

title: Add BuildTarget=WrappedComServer project and host DTO support
description: Delivery bead to add BuildTarget=WrappedComServer to project and host DTO surfaces. Outcome: .basproj, generated project files, CLI/direct-host settings, and capability status can represent the wrapped COM server target truthfully.

Add WrappedComServer enum value and optional WrapperComServer alias if bd-wcs1.1.2 specifies it. Update parse/generate/load/host_helpers/CLI display and tests. Add Windows-only/bitness/toolchain/registration disabled reasons to host-facing DTOs where this bead scopes them, or leave explicit follow-up fields for bd-wcs1.9.3.
acceptance_criteria: parse/generate roundtrip tests cover WrappedComServer; host project settings edit/apply supports it; CLI init/build help does not overclaim execution; non-Windows availability is typed; governance and project tests pass.

Evidence: cargo test -p oxvba-project --quiet; cargo check -p oxvba-project -p oxvba-cli -p oxvba-host --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-cli default_build_output_path --quiet; ./scripts/check-governance.ps1.

title: Epic: wrapped late-bound COM server DLL
description: Delivery epic for COM-0007: a real late-bound WrappedComServer DLL. Scope is not source generation alone; oxvba build must emit a Windows in-process COM server DLL that external clients can register/load/CreateObject and invoke through IDispatch into OxVba objects.
design: Expected before: crates/oxvba-build/src/comserver.rs emits skeleton exports and crates/oxvba-build/src/registration.rs/typelib_gen.rs exist, but GetIDsOfNames/Invoke do not route to Engine descriptors. Implementation should keep generated DLL thin: load embedded/sidecar .oxb, bootstrap Engine/runtime flavor, maintain object identity/refcounts, implement DllGetClassObject/DllCanUnloadNow/DllRegisterServer/DllUnregisterServer, IClassFactory, IUnknown, IDispatch, and error support through stable helper APIs.
acceptance_criteria: COM-0007 can be evidenced by a controlled Windows client: registration/load succeeds, CreateObject returns the wrapped class, methods/properties/default members/object returns/arrays/supported errors execute through OxVba, and failure HRESULT/EXCEPINFO behavior is deterministic.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-build/src/comserver.rs, comserver_exe.rs, registration.rs, dll.rs, typelib_gen.rs; crates/oxvba-host/src/engine.rs Engine::create_class_instance and invoke_member_on_object_with_variants; docs/spec/BASPROJ_SPEC_V1.md section 5.6; COM-0007 row.
close_reason: COM-0007 wrapped late-bound COM server DLL lane complete for the controlled Windows scope. The generated WrappedComServer DLL builds with standard COM exports, creates class instances through Engine, resolves and invokes IDispatch members by descriptor/call-frame metadata, covers method/property/default/object/array/error behavior, and now supports per-user DllRegisterServer/DllUnregisterServer plus CLSIDFromProgID/CoCreateInstance registered activation evidence. Matrix/evidence/workset truth updated; reusable COM-0007 script and governance pass.

title: Compile generated WrappedComServer DLL skeleton with COM exports
description: Delivery bead to compile a generated WrappedComServer DLL skeleton with standard COM exports. Outcome: oxvba-build can produce a Windows cdylib/DLL artifact for one creatable class, even before full invocation behavior is wired.
design: Expected before: comserver.rs emits skeleton source but oxvba build does not compile/publish/register a usable DLL. Decide generated Rust/C/C++ path consistent with existing oxvba-build/dll helpers; embed or sidecar .oxb; emit DllMain, DllGetClassObject, DllCanUnloadNow, DllRegisterServer, DllUnregisterServer, export definitions, and build logs. Make failures deterministic on non-Windows/missing toolchain. Keep skeleton honest: if Invoke is still unsupported, tests must assert explicit unsupported behavior, not success.
acceptance_criteria: Windows-only build test or guarded integration builds a DLL and verifies exported symbols; non-Windows test reports typed unsupported/disabled state; artifact paths are returned to CLI/host; no COM-0007 completion claim yet.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-build/src/comserver.rs, dll.rs, registration.rs; crates/oxvba-build/tests/com_attribute_export_end_to_end.rs; docs/spec/WINDOWS_FIXED_EXPORT_HOSTS_V1.md section around COM server DLL distinction.
close_reason: Done: added compile_wrapped_com_server_shim with typed Windows-only behavior, wired oxvba build BuildTarget=WrappedComServer to produce a DLL artifact path, defaulted WrappedComServer outputs to .dll, and updated generated COM server source for Rust 2024 unsafe export attributes. Windows test compiles a generated cdylib and verifies DllGetClassObject, DllCanUnloadNow, DllRegisterServer, and DllUnregisterServer export names in the PE; non-Windows has a typed UnsupportedPlatform result. Docs state this is skeleton artifact production only, not COM-0007 dispatch completion. Evidence: cargo test -p oxvba-build wrapped_com_server_build_compiles_dll_with_standard_exports --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-build com_server --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-cli default_build_output_path --quiet; cargo check -p oxvba-build -p oxvba-cli --quiet; ./scripts/check-governance.ps1.

title: Implement IClassFactory over Engine class creation
description: Delivery bead to implement IClassFactory over Engine class creation. Outcome: DllGetClassObject returns a class factory whose CreateInstance creates wrapped OxVba object instances for creatable classes.
design: Expected before: Engine::create_class_instance exists and ComServer project validation identifies creatable classes, but class factory skeleton is not wired. Implement CLSID -> class descriptor lookup from bundle metadata, IClassFactory::QueryInterface/AddRef/Release/CreateInstance/LockServer, no-aggregation handling (CLASS_E_NOAGGREGATION), class-not-registered/no-interface failures, and DllCanUnloadNow lock/object counting. Ensure created objects share runtime object identity/projection core and call Class_Initialize.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled Windows/Rust COM client can call DllGetClassObject/CreateInstance for a creatable CLSID; non-creatable/private class fails deterministically; LockServer affects DllCanUnloadNow; object lifecycle tests prove initialize path; no Invoke success required until bd-wcs1.5.3.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-host/src/engine.rs create_class_instance; crates/oxvba-project/src/validate.rs ComServer validation; runtime object identity bd-wcs1.2; Win32 IClassFactory semantics.
close_reason: Done: generated IClassFactory::CreateInstance now deserializes the embedded bundle, prepares an Engine runtime session, calls Engine::create_class_instance for the requested creatable class, and stores the resulting ObjectRef/session on the dispatch instance. Engine class initialization now passes implicit Me into Class_Initialize when needed. Controlled Windows test loads the generated DLL, calls DllGetClassObject, exercises LockServer/DllCanUnloadNow, calls CreateInstance for IID_IDispatch, and releases object/factory; Invoke remains unsupported until bd-wcs1.5.3. Evidence: cargo test -p oxvba-build wrapped_com_server_build_compiles_dll_with_standard_exports --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-host --test invoke_procedure_tests create_class --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-build com_server_has --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-host --lib engine::tests --quiet; cargo check -p oxvba-build -p oxvba-host --quiet; ./scripts/check-governance.ps1.

title: Implement IDispatch names and invoke over descriptors
description: Delivery bead to implement IDispatch names and Invoke over descriptors/call frames. Outcome: wrapped objects can resolve case-insensitive names to DISPIDs and execute methods/properties/default members through OxVba Engine using RuntimeCallFrame.
design: Expected before: class factory can create wrapper objects, call-frame and COM marshaling helpers exist, but GetIDsOfNames/Invoke are skeleton. Implement GetTypeInfoCount/GetTypeInfo where scoped, GetIDsOfNames case-insensitive member/argument name mapping, stable DISPIDs from descriptors, Invoke for DISPATCH_METHOD/PROPERTYGET/PROPERTYPUT/PROPERTYPUTREF, reverse DISPPARAMS arg order, named args, default member, byref writeback, pVarResult, EXCEPINFO, pArgErr, IErrorInfo/ISupportErrorInfo if in scope, and RuntimeCallError -> HRESULT mapping. Use Engine::invoke_member... or newer call-frame API; do not reparse source.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/integration tests cover method, property get/let/set, default member, missing member, arity/type mismatch with pArgErr, runtime Err to EXCEPINFO, object and array return, and case-insensitive names. This is the first behavior bead that can make COM-0007 nearly complete but still needs external evidence in bd-wcs1.5.4.
notes: Pointers: crates/oxvba-com/src/windows_invoke.rs and windows_variant.rs; Engine invocation hooks; MS-OAUT IDispatch anchors; existing com_client_end_to_end tests for external COM client behavior.
close_reason: Done: generated IDispatch::GetIDsOfNames now resolves member names from emitted descriptor tables, and IDispatch::Invoke now lowers DISPPARAMS through oxvba-com call-frame helpers, calls Engine::invoke_member_on_object_with_variants on the wrapped object, and marshals RuntimeCallResult back to VARIANT/EXCEPINFO. Controlled Windows DLL test resolves Ping, invokes it through IDispatch, and observes the Class_Initialize-backed Long result. Broader object/array/error evidence remains for bd-wcs1.5.4. Evidence: cargo test -p oxvba-build wrapped_com_server_build_compiles_dll_with_standard_exports --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-build com_server_has --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-com windows_call_frame --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-host --test invoke_procedure_tests create_class --quiet; cargo check -p oxvba-build -p oxvba-host -p oxvba-com --quiet; ./scripts/check-governance.ps1.

title: Capture controlled Windows late-bound WrappedComServer evidence

Add a controlled sample project and script, preferably per-user/test-scope registration, then run a Rust/Win32, PowerShell, or VBA late-bound client. Capture commands, stdout/stderr, registry/registration plan, DLL/TLB paths if present, and result CSV/summary. Exercise method, property get/let/set, default member, object return, array return, and supported error path. If Office is unavailable, use controlled COM client for COM-0007 and leave Office-specific claims to COM-0008/0010.

title: Expand WrappedComServer late-bound dispatch breadth beyond scalar method slice

Implement deterministic DllRegisterServer/DllUnregisterServer behavior for CLSID/ProgID/InprocServer32 metadata or a documented activation-equivalent test harness, then evidence CreateObject/CoCreateInstance returning the wrapped class and invoking the already-proved late-bound method/property/default/object/array/error surface. title: Epic: typelib and dispatch-backed early binding

Implementation should generate library/coclass/default-interface/source-interface metadata from persisted descriptors, register or sidecar the TLB, and add both introspection and Office/VBA client evidence.

title: Generate and register TLB for one wrapped class
description: Delivery bead to generate and register/load a TLB for one wrapped class. Outcome: typelib generation consumes bundle descriptors and emits metadata matching the wrapped COM server classes/interfaces/members.

title: Review and fix WrappedComServer typelib signature export fidelity
description:
Delivery bug bead for WrappedComServer typelib export fidelity.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build a WrappedComServer project with interface method `Public Function AddThem(ByVal leftValue As Double, ByVal rightValue As Double) As Double` and a creatable class implementing it.
2. Load the generated TLB and inspect `AddThem` parameter and return metadata.
3. Register the generated DLL and consume it from an early-bound VBA/OxVBA client using `Dim calc As IMyCalc`, `Set calc = New MyCalc`, and `resultValue = calc.AddThem(1.25, 2.5)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generated TLB exposes `AddThem` with two `Double` inputs and a `Double` retval instead of generic `VARIANT` entries.
- WrappedComServer build/register path produces a TLB the early-bound client can reference.
- Early-bound client observes `3.75` for `calc.AddThem(1.25, 2.5)`.
- Existing controlled wrapped COM and typelib checks remain green.
- If full typed Automation coverage remains broader than this bead, the supported scalar subset is documented and follow-up beads are created for residual types.

## Notes
Review the descriptor pipeline from compiler procedure metadata through `ComClassExportDescriptor` / `DispatchMemberInfo`, `typelib_gen.rs`, `idl.rs`, registration, and wrapped `IDispatch` return marshaling. Preserve supported parameter VARTYPEs and retval VARTYPEs instead of defaulting blindly to `VARIANT`.
notes:
Implemented typed WrappedComServer typelib signature export pipeline.

title: Activation-frame model: per-call slot windows for recursion and return temporary lifetime
description:
## Outcome

Delivery bead: introduce real per-call activation frames/slot windows so recursive calls preserve caller locals and procedure-local object references leave scope at the correct time.

This is the residual split out of `bd-1ufc`. `bd-1ufc` owns per-instance object fields and same-box teardown; this bead owns the flat-register execution model.

## Current failure

The VM uses one flat `RegisterFile.registers: Vec<RuntimeSlot>` and `call_stack` saves only `(return_pc, error_frame)`. The compiler allocates globally unique slots across procedures, but recursive calls to the same procedure reuse the same parameter/local/temporary/return slots. This breaks recursion and keeps callee return/object slots alive longer than VBA statement/procedure lifetimes.

Observed probes:
- `recursion_preserves_caller_locals` is ignored; `Fact(5)` returns `16`, not `120`.
- VBA oracle probe B expects `gMT`; OxVba currently proves member dispatch as `gM` but the trailing `T` is pinned by the callee return slot.

## Scope

- VM register access: add activation frame state and resolve frame-relative procedure slots through the current frame base/window.
- Call/return paths: `CallProc`, inline project-member calls, `invoke_*_with_slots`, debug resume/step paths, and error unwinding must push/pop frames consistently.
- Compiler/package metadata: emit procedure-local slots as frame-relative and carry each procedure frame size, parameter slots, return slot, temp slots, and any static/module/global slots separately.
- Calling convention: copy/move ByVal args and return values across frame boundaries; preserve ByRef alias semantics explicitly rather than accidentally through shared global slot indices.
- Snapshot/debugger surfaces: expose entry/module/global slots and active frame locals intentionally, not by slicing the flat register file.

## Non-goals

- Per-instance class field storage and same-box `Class_Terminate` teardown; tracked by `bd-1ufc`.
- Full front-end/binder replacement, though the slot contract must be compatible with the planned front-end rework.
design:
## Implemented shape

The VM now keeps procedure-local slots in activation-frame overlays instead of treating every procedure slot as one process-wide register. Each active call owns a `HashMap<slot, RuntimeSlot>` for the slots declared in that procedure's runtime metadata. Read/write helpers resolve through the current frame first and fall back to the retained global register file for module/static/global surfaces.

Calls now transfer values across frame boundaries explicitly:
- descriptor-backed early calls evaluate arguments into caller-side source slots; the VM reads those values before pushing the callee frame, pushes the frame, then binds parameter slots inside the callee frame;
- descriptor-less expression calls keep the legacy bytecode convention, and the VM bridges existing parameter/return slots across the new frame boundary as a compatibility path;
- return values and ByRef writebacks are captured while the callee frame is current, then written into the caller frame after pop;
- descriptor-less expression-call fallback return slots are cleared after copy so object returns do not leave a second retained reference behind the receiver temp.

Statement-boundary temporary cleanup and procedure epilogue cleanup now operate against the current frame, so object temporaries release at VBA statement granularity while recursive calls preserve caller locals.

Fast integer/copy/compare shortcuts bail out for framed slots, forcing the frame-aware slow path when a procedure-local slot is involved.

## Evidence

- `recursion_preserves_caller_locals` is unignored and passes: `Fact(5) == 120`.
- `member_access_on_function_call_result_dispatches` now asserts the full Excel oracle order `gMT`.
- Existing `pure_oxvba_class` coverage remains green after `bd-1ufc` and this bead.
- Bundle tests and workspace test compile pass.

## Known residuals

No material residual remains for this bead's scoped recursion/return-temporary behavior. The broader front-end rework can replace the compatibility bridge with fully described call-site metadata for expression calls later.
acceptance_criteria:
Close when all are true:

- `recursion_preserves_caller_locals` is unignored and passes with `Fact(5) == 120`.
- The `MakeFoo().Tag & Mark()` lifetime probe is strengthened from `gM` to `gMT` and passes.
- Existing Class_Terminate timing tests still pass, including the object-field cascade once `bd-1ufc` is complete.
- ByVal, ByRef, function return, host direct invocation, debug stepping, and error-handler return paths have focused regression coverage or updated existing coverage.
- Compiler/runtime package metadata documents the frame-relative slot contract and separates module/global storage from procedure activation storage.
- Relevant checks pass: at minimum focused `oxvba-compiler`, `oxvba-vm`, and `oxvba-host` tests that cover call/return/recursion/lifetime behavior.
- Fresh-eyes review records no remaining material issues in frame pop ordering, return-value transfer, ByRef aliasing, or debug/snapshot behavior.
close_reason: Implemented activation-frame slot overlays and call/return transfer for recursive calls and return temporary lifetime. Evidence: recursion_preserves_caller_locals unignored and passes; member_access_on_function_call_result_dispatches now asserts/passes gMT; cargo test -p oxvba-host pure_oxvba_class --quiet; cargo test -p oxvba-compiler bundle --quiet; cargo check --workspace --tests --quiet. Fresh-eyes review found no debug leftovers or ignored residual for this bead; governance still has unrelated ODG-049 foldback failure.

title: Fixed-size-array Erase: reset elements (not deallocate) via runtime FADF_FIXEDSIZE
description: vm3 ArrayErase stores Empty for ALL arrays (correct for dynamic, WRONG for fixed-size: real VBA reinitializes fixed-array elements to defaults and keeps the array usable). vm3 is the oracle now so it must be correct, not vm2-faithful. User-approved design: carry FADF_FIXEDSIZE (0x0010) on the array VALUE (vm3 SafeArray), set at allocation, preserved through copies/params; Erase dispatches on the array's own flag exactly like real VBA. Full plan + the design question to validate first (runtime value-flag vs static type-system extension; OxVBA limitation vs VBA limitation) + broader SafeArray fidelity (ReDim-of-fixed rejection, COM marshaling FADF) + acceptance criteria in docs/SAFEARRAY_FIXED_ARRAY_ERASE_HANDOVER.md. Surfaced after W14, post vm2-deletion.
